```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 13, fig.height = 8)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(furrr)
library(digest)
library(igraph)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
source(here::here("scripts/Network.R"))
dir.create(here::here("reports/Report_23_files/figure-gfm"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(here::here("data"), showWarnings = FALSE)

N_WORKERS <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1)

TIMING_LOG <- list()

run_cached <- function(cache_name, fn, hash_obj) {
  hash       <- digest::digest(hash_obj)
  cache_file <- here::here(paste0("data/", cache_name, "_cache.rds"))
  if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
    cc <- readRDS(cache_file)
    if (identical(cc$hash, hash)) {
      message(sprintf("[%s] cache hit", cache_name))
      # n_rows = one row per (grid cell, seed) in every raw sweep this wraps,
      # i.e. exactly the number of simulate_liquid_democracy() calls that
      # cache represents -- tracked even on a cache hit (loaded, not
      # recomputed) so Sec 11 can show "how many runs" alongside "how long",
      # not just for freshly-computed rows.
      n_rows <- if (is.data.frame(cc$data)) nrow(cc$data) else NA_integer_
      TIMING_LOG[[length(TIMING_LOG) + 1]] <<- tibble(cache_name = cache_name, seconds = 0, status = "cached", n_rows = n_rows)
      return(cc$data)
    }
  }
  t0  <- Sys.time()
  out <- fn()
  dt  <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))
  message(sprintf("[%s] computed in %.1fs", cache_name, dt))
  n_rows <- if (is.data.frame(out)) nrow(out) else NA_integer_
  TIMING_LOG[[length(TIMING_LOG) + 1]] <<- tibble(cache_name = cache_name, seconds = dt, status = "computed", n_rows = n_rows)
  saveRDS(list(hash = hash, data = out), cache_file)
  out
}

metrics_core   <- c("delegation_stability", "delegation_rate", "lost_vote_rate", "chain_length", "top5_power_share", "share_50pct")
metric_labels  <- c(delegation_stability = "Delegation stability", delegation_rate = "Delegation rate",
                     lost_vote_rate = "Lost-vote rate", chain_length = "Avg. chain length",
                     top5_power_share = "Top-5% voting-power share", share_50pct = "Voters for 50% power")
metrics_r <- c("delegation_rate", "delegation_stability", "lost_vote_rate", "top5_power_share", "share_50pct", "chain_length")

RATE_METRICS_01 <- c("Delegation stability", "Delegation rate", "Lost-vote rate", "Top-5% voting-power share", "Voters for 50% power")

y_anchor_01 <- function(metric_factor_levels, x_val) {
  present <- intersect(RATE_METRICS_01, metric_factor_levels)
  if (!length(present)) return(tibble(metric = factor(character(0), levels = metric_factor_levels), y = numeric(0), x = numeric(0)))
  tidyr::crossing(metric = factor(present, levels = metric_factor_levels), y = c(0, 1), x = x_val)
}

FACET_SPACING <- theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(1, "cm"))

steady_state_per_seed <- function(raw_df, round_max, window, id_cols, metrics = metrics_core) {
  raw_df |>
    filter(round > round_max - window) |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(metrics), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
    group_by(across(all_of(c(id_cols, "metric")))) |>
    summarise(steady_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}
steady_state_summary <- function(per_seed_df, group_cols) {
  per_seed_df |>
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_cols, "metric")))) |>
    summarise(mean_val = mean(steady_val, na.rm = TRUE),
              sd_val   = sd(steady_val, na.rm = TRUE),
              n_val    = sum(!is.na(steady_val)),
              se_val   = sd_val / sqrt(n_val), .groups = "drop")
}

find_saturation_point <- function(sub, value_col, x_col, frac = 0.01, relative = FALSE, hold = 3) {
  sub <- sub[order(sub[[x_col]]), ]
  d <- abs(c(NA, diff(sub[[value_col]])))
  if (relative) {
    peak <- suppressWarnings(max(d, na.rm = TRUE))
    if (!is.finite(peak)) return(NA_real_)
    if (peak == 0) return(sub[[x_col]][1])
    thresh <- frac * peak
  } else {
    thresh <- frac
  }
  ok <- !is.na(d) & d < thresh
  n  <- length(ok)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    window_end <- min(i + hold - 1, n)
    if (all(ok[i:window_end])) return(sub[[x_col]][i])
  }
  NA_real_
}

# effect_pct_to_r() (automatic pct-of-saturated-effect -> r translation, via
# a derivative/threshold-based curve search) is RETIRED. Three iterations of
# automatic fixes each solved one failure mode and introduced another: (1) a
# fixed absolute delta threshold was miscalibrated for metrics outside [0,1]
# (e.g. Avg. chain length); (2) a short "hold for the next few points"
# forward-crossing search was fooled by a genuine, SUSTAINED overshoot
# spanning several consecutive grid points (r_pw's Avg. chain length in
# [0.2, 2.0]); (3) requiring the crossing to hold all the way through to
# r_sat instead became sensitive to a single late seed-noise blip anywhere
# in [0, r_sat], pushing even low-percentage targets out to implausibly
# large r.
#
# Replaced with a hybrid: a human picks r_sat AND which metric it's read off
# (by eye, from the diagnostic table/plot after each isolated-dimension
# sweep, Sec 2.2/4.2) -- the one genuinely ambiguous judgement call, now
# made explicitly rather than by a threshold heuristic. Given that anchor,
# pct_to_r_from_anchor() does a straightforward VALUE-based inverse
# interpolation (target_val = y0 + pct/100*(y_sat-y0), then approx() finds
# the r_val where the curve crosses target_val) restricted to r <= r_sat --
# safe specifically because the human's own choice of r_sat is exactly the
# claim "the curve behaves well (monotonic-enough) up to here", which is the
# one thing the automatic version couldn't verify for itself. Percentages
# are therefore genuine percentages of the metric's own value range (e.g.
# "50%" means the metric is exactly halfway from its r=0 value to its
# r_sat value), not a linear split of the r-axis.
pct_to_r_from_anchor <- function(dim_name, pct, curve, anchor_tbl) {
  r_sat_d  <- anchor_tbl$r_sat[anchor_tbl$dim == dim_name]
  metric_d <- anchor_tbl$r_sat_metric[anchor_tbl$dim == dim_name]
  sub <- curve |>
    filter(dim == dim_name, metric == metric_d, r_val <= r_sat_d) |>
    arrange(r_val)
  if (nrow(sub) < 2) return(rep(NA_real_, length(pct)))
  y0 <- sub$mean_val[1]; y_sat <- sub$mean_val[nrow(sub)]
  # A completely flat curve (y0 == y_sat) has no well-posed "% of the way
  # there" -- approx() would error on it directly (collapses to a single
  # unique x value, needs >=2 to interpolate). Confirmed to actually happen
  # in Report_23.Rmd (Delegation rate flat across the whole r_ig range at
  # r_op=r_pw=r_tr=0); falls back to r=0 for every pct rather than crashing.
  if (isTRUE(all.equal(y0, y_sat))) return(rep(sub$r_val[1], length(pct)))
  target_val <- y0 + pct / 100 * (y_sat - y0)
  sub_by_val <- sub |> arrange(mean_val)
  approx(sub_by_val$mean_val, sub_by_val$r_val, xout = target_val, rule = 2)$y
}

# Compact diagnostic tables for the by-eye read-off (Sec 2.2, 4.2): one
# table per dimension (own r_val grid -- pw's is denser near zero than
# op/tr's), each metric abbreviated to keep 6 metrics x (value + delta)
# readable as columns, delta shown right next to its value column instead
# of as the separate step-to-step-delta section this replaces (former Sec
# 4.3, retired -- its content now lives here instead of duplicated).
METRIC_ABBR <- setNames(c("DR", "DS", "LV", "T5", "V50", "CL"),
                        unname(metric_labels[metrics_r]))

build_diag_tables <- function(summary_df) {
  make_one <- function(dim_name) {
    df <- summary_df |>
      filter(dim == dim_name) |>
      mutate(abbr = METRIC_ABBR[as.character(metric)]) |>
      arrange(abbr, r_val) |>
      group_by(abbr) |>
      # Delta as % of the metric's OWN observed range (max-min across r_val),
      # not an absolute difference -- the same scale-mismatch problem as the
      # old fixed-0.01 saturation threshold: an absolute delta of, say,
      # 0.01 is a huge step for a metric ranging 0-1 but negligible for one
      # ranging 1-3.5 (e.g. Avg. chain length). Normalising by each metric's
      # own range makes "has this basically stopped moving" comparable
      # across metrics again.
      mutate(rng   = diff(range(mean_val, na.rm = TRUE)),
             delta = if_else(rng > 0, (mean_val - lag(mean_val)) / rng * 100, NA_real_)) |>
      ungroup()
    r_vals <- sort(unique(df$r_val))
    out <- tibble(r_val = r_vals)
    for (a in unname(METRIC_ABBR)) {
      sub <- df |> filter(abbr == a) |> arrange(r_val)
      out[[a]]              <- sub$mean_val[match(r_vals, sub$r_val)]
      out[[paste0(a, "_d")]] <- sub$delta[match(r_vals, sub$r_val)]
    }
    out
  }
  list(op = make_one("op"), pw = make_one("pw"), tr = make_one("tr"))
}

# Readable display headers for a build_diag_tables() table -- kable's
# col.names overrides only the DISPLAYED header, not the underlying (unique,
# valid) column names the data frame itself still needs internally.
METRIC_DISPLAY <- c(DR = "Del. Rate", DS = "Del. Stab.", LV = "Lost Votes",
                    T5 = "Top 5%", V50 = "Voters 50%", CL = "Chain Len.")
diag_col_names <- function(tbl) {
  nm <- names(tbl)[-1]
  disp <- vapply(nm, function(n) if (grepl("_d$", n)) "Delta %" else unname(METRIC_DISPLAY[n]), character(1))
  c("r_val", disp)
}

# Value columns need more decimal places (metrics like CDR can sit at
# 0.0003) than delta columns (now a %, 1 decimal is plenty).
round_diag_table <- function(tbl) {
  tbl |>
    mutate(across(-c(r_val, ends_with("_d")), ~round(.x, 4)),
           across(ends_with("_d"), ~round(.x, 1)))
}

N_BASE <- 1000L

lambda_from_forget_rate <- function(forget_pct, h = 5) 1 - (1 - forget_pct / 100)^(1 / h)
LAMBDA_FORGET_PCT_5 <- 50   # target: % of trust signal forgotten over 5 voting rounds
LAMBDA_CONTEXT <- lambda_from_forget_rate(LAMBDA_FORGET_PCT_5, h = 5)
```

# 2. Attractiveness-threshold validation (the K decision)

## 2.1 Definition

For agent $i$ and neighbour $j$, $j$ qualifies as a usable delegation
target if j is at least `tolerance` as attractive as i is to itself:
$A_{ij} \geq \text{tolerance} \cdot A_{ii}$. Since `attractiveness_expose()`
gives $A_{ii} \equiv 1$ always (opinion distance 0, power ratio 1), this is
equivalent to $A_{ij} \geq \text{tolerance}$ directly. Report 22 used
tolerance = 1 (j must be at least as attractive as i itself) -- here three
looser tolerance levels are compared instead: 20%, 50%, 80%.

```{r p2-rsweep-config}
R_OPTR_MAX <- c(0, 2^(0:15))
R_PW_VALS  <- c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.2), 2^(2:15))

R_ISOLATED_GRID <- bind_rows(
  tibble(dim = "op", r_val = R_OPTR_MAX),
  tibble(dim = "pw", r_val = R_PW_VALS),
  tibble(dim = "tr", r_val = R_OPTR_MAX)
)

N_SEEDS_R <- 25L
SAT_ABS_THRESH         <- 0.01
SAT_HOLD_POINTS        <- 3
FINE_GRID_RATIO_THRESH <- 0.1
```

```{r p2-rsweep-fn}
run_r_sweep <- function(K_val, T_val, NV_val, cache_tag) {
  run_r_cell <- function(seed, N, K, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) {
    window <- max(1, T_val - 4):T_val
    res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
      seed = seed, n_per_community = N, n_communities = 1, node_degree = K, T = T_val,
      n_voting_rounds = NV_val,
      r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_CONTEXT, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
      self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
      sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05,
      snap_rounds = window
    )
    snap_idx <- match(window, res$snapshots$round)
    tibble(
      seed = seed, round = window,
      delegation_rate      = res$history_delegation[window],
      delegation_stability = res$history_stability[window],
      lost_vote_rate       = res$history_lost[window],
      top5_power_share     = res$snapshots$top5_power_share[snap_idx],
      share_50pct          = res$snapshots$share_50pct[snap_idx],
      chain_length         = res$snapshots$avg_chain_length_delegators[snap_idx]
    )
  }

  run_isolated_cell <- function(seed, dim, r_val) {
    r_op <- if (dim == "op") r_val else 0
    r_pw <- if (dim == "pw") r_val else 0
    r_tr <- if (dim == "tr") r_val else 0
    run_r_cell(seed, N_BASE, K_val, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) |> mutate(dim = dim, r_val = r_val, .before = 1)
  }

  grid_r_isolated <- R_ISOLATED_GRID |> tidyr::crossing(seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_R))

  r3_isolated_raw <- run_cached(paste0("r23r_isolated_raw_", cache_tag), function() {
    plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
    out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_r_isolated, function(dim, r_val, seed) run_isolated_cell(seed, dim, r_val),
                            .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
    plan(sequential)
    out
  }, list(R_ISOLATED_GRID, N_SEEDS_R, K_val, T_val, NV_val, LAMBDA_CONTEXT, v = 2))

  r3_isolated_summary <- steady_state_summary(
    steady_state_per_seed(r3_isolated_raw, T_val, 5L, c("dim", "r_val", "seed"), metrics = metrics_r),
    c("dim", "r_val")
  ) |> mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels[metrics_r])))

  # r_sat per dimension = MAX saturation point ACROSS ALL METRICS (Report 22
  # only checked "Delegation rate"). A dimension counts as saturated only
  # once EVERY tracked metric has individually stopped changing -- same
  # "max across metrics" principle already used for nv/dt in run_t_sweep()
  # (Sec 3). An un-saturated metric (NA) is capped at the max swept r-value
  # rather than dropped by na.rm, so it correctly drives the ceiling up
  # instead of being silently ignored.
  # SAT_HOLD_POINTS (find_saturation_point()'s "hold" arg): a candidate point
  # only needs the NEXT `hold` deltas to stay below SAT_ABS_THRESH, not every
  # remaining point out to r=32768. Without this, a single noisy seed-driven
  # blip anywhere in the tail (even between two irrelevantly-high r-values)
  # makes the whole metric return NA -> gets capped to 32768 -> wins the
  # slice_max() below against a genuinely-detected, much smaller r_sat.
  # SAT_ABS_THRESH is scaled by each metric's OWN observed range (mean_val
  # span within that dim x metric curve) before being passed to
  # find_saturation_point() as an absolute frac. A single fixed absolute
  # threshold (e.g. 0.01) is only meaningful for metrics bounded in [0,1]
  # (delegation rate, lost-vote rate, stability, top5 share, share_50pct);
  # "Avg. chain length" ranges ~1-3.5 (span ~2.5), so the same 0.01 delta is
  # proportionally ~2.5x stricter there and gets defeated by ordinary
  # seed-sampling noise, spuriously never satisfying the "flat" criterion.
  # Since that made chain length win slice_max() below for every dimension
  # regardless of whether it genuinely saturates latest, r_sat was landing
  # on (or near) the grid's max value for pw/tr by construction rather than
  # by finding, which this per-curve rescaling (same principle already
  # used by effect_pct_to_r()'s pct-of-own-range target) corrects.
  r_sat_per_metric <- function(df) {
    df |>
      group_by(dim, metric) |>
      group_modify(~ {
        span   <- diff(range(.x$mean_val, na.rm = TRUE))
        thresh <- if (is.finite(span) && span > 0) SAT_ABS_THRESH * span else SAT_ABS_THRESH
        tibble(r_sat = find_saturation_point(.x, "mean_val", "r_val", frac = thresh, relative = FALSE, hold = SAT_HOLD_POINTS))
      }) |>
      ungroup() |>
      mutate(r_sat_capped = ifelse(is.na(r_sat), max(R_OPTR_MAX), r_sat)) |>
      group_by(dim) |>
      slice_max(r_sat_capped, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
      ungroup() |>
      transmute(dim, r_sat = r_sat_capped, r_sat_metric = as.character(metric))
  }

  r_sat_coarse <- r_sat_per_metric(r3_isolated_summary)

  r_sat_ref   <- max(r_sat_coarse$r_sat, na.rm = TRUE)
  dim_slowest <- r_sat_coarse$dim[which.max(r_sat_coarse$r_sat)]
  N_FINE      <- sum(R_OPTR_MAX <= r_sat_ref)

  dims_needing_fine <- r_sat_coarse |>
    filter(dim != dim_slowest, r_sat < FINE_GRID_RATIO_THRESH * r_sat_ref) |>
    pull(dim)
  coarse_keep_dims <- setdiff(c("op", "pw", "tr"), dims_needing_fine)

  build_fine_grid <- function(dim_name) {
    r_sat_d <- r_sat_coarse$r_sat[r_sat_coarse$dim == dim_name]
    if (is.na(r_sat_d)) r_sat_d <- max(R_OPTR_MAX)
    tibble(dim = dim_name, r_val = seq(0, r_sat_d, length.out = N_FINE))
  }

  r3_isolated_final <- r3_isolated_summary |>
    filter(dim %in% coarse_keep_dims) |>
    left_join(r_sat_coarse, by = "dim") |>
    filter(r_val <= ifelse(is.na(r_sat), max(R_OPTR_MAX), r_sat)) |>
    select(-r_sat, -r_sat_metric)

  if (length(dims_needing_fine) > 0) {
    R_ISOLATED_GRID_FINE <- bind_rows(lapply(dims_needing_fine, build_fine_grid))
    grid_r_isolated_fine <- R_ISOLATED_GRID_FINE |> tidyr::crossing(seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_R))

    r3_isolated_raw_fine <- run_cached(paste0("r23r_isolated_raw_fine_", cache_tag), function() {
      plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
      out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_r_isolated_fine, function(dim, r_val, seed) run_isolated_cell(seed, dim, r_val),
                              .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
      plan(sequential)
      out
    }, list(R_ISOLATED_GRID_FINE, N_SEEDS_R, K_val, T_val, NV_val, LAMBDA_CONTEXT, v = 2))

    r3_isolated_summary_fine <- steady_state_summary(
      steady_state_per_seed(r3_isolated_raw_fine, T_val, 5L, c("dim", "r_val", "seed"), metrics = metrics_r),
      c("dim", "r_val")
    ) |> mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels[metrics_r])))

    r3_isolated_final <- bind_rows(r3_isolated_final, r3_isolated_summary_fine)
  }

  r_sat_isolated <- r_sat_per_metric(r3_isolated_final)

  list(r_sat_coarse = r_sat_coarse, dims_needing_fine = dims_needing_fine,
       coarse_keep_dims = coarse_keep_dims, dim_slowest = dim_slowest,
       r3_isolated_summary = r3_isolated_summary, r3_isolated_final = r3_isolated_final,
       r_sat_isolated = r_sat_isolated)
}
```

```{r p2-bootstrap-run}
K_BOOTSTRAP  <- 40L
T_BOOTSTRAP  <- 30L
NV_BOOTSTRAP <- 10L

bootstrap_r_res <- run_r_sweep(K_BOOTSTRAP, T_BOOTSTRAP, NV_BOOTSTRAP, "bootstrap")
```

## 2.2 Independent effect-percentage r-triples

```{r p2-bootstrap-isolated-plot, fig.height=9}
bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(r_val, mean_val, colour = dim, group = dim)) +
  geom_blank(data = y_anchor_01(levels(bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_summary$metric), x_val = 1),
             aes(x = x, y = y), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log1p", breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768)) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "dimension", end = 0.85,
                          labels = c(op = "r_op", pw = "r_pw", tr = "r_tr")) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "Isolated responsiveness dimensions (bootstrap r-sweep) -- other two held at r=0",
       subtitle = sprintf("K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d, N=%d, %d seed(s) per point; r swept up to %d; x on log1p scale",
                           K_BOOTSTRAP, T_BOOTSTRAP, NV_BOOTSTRAP, N_BASE, N_SEEDS_R, max(R_OPTR_MAX)),
       x = "r value (log1p scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") + FACET_SPACING
```

"Delta %" columns = step-to-step change as a % of that metric's own
observed range (max-min across all r_val), not an absolute difference --
comparable across metrics regardless of their scale (replaces the former
separate step-to-step-delta section).

```{r p2-diag-table}
diag_bootstrap <- build_diag_tables(bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_summary)

kable(round_diag_table(diag_bootstrap$op), col.names = diag_col_names(diag_bootstrap$op),
      caption = "`r_op`, bootstrap r-sweep -- read off by eye where the slowest metric stops changing further; use this to set `R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP` below")
kable(round_diag_table(diag_bootstrap$pw), col.names = diag_col_names(diag_bootstrap$pw),
      caption = "`r_pw`, bootstrap r-sweep")
kable(round_diag_table(diag_bootstrap$tr), col.names = diag_col_names(diag_bootstrap$tr),
      caption = "`r_tr`, bootstrap r-sweep")
```

```{r p2-sat-anchor-manual}
# ANNAHME (read off by eye from the table/plot above): for each dimension,
# the r_val at which ITS OWN slowest-to-settle metric stops changing further
# (r_sat), and which metric that is. This is the one genuinely ambiguous
# judgement call -- everything below (the pct_ref_table percentages) is then
# a value-based interpolation ON that metric's own curve, restricted to
# r <= r_sat, via pct_to_r_from_anchor() (see its comment above).
R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP <- tribble(
  ~dim,  ~r_sat, ~r_sat_metric,
  "op",  16384,  "Delegation rate",
  "pw",  64,     "Top-5% voting-power share",
  "tr",  128,    "Delegation rate"
)

pct_ref_table <- tibble(pct = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) |>
  mutate(
    r_op = pct_to_r_from_anchor("op", pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_pw = pct_to_r_from_anchor("pw", pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_tr = pct_to_r_from_anchor("tr", pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP)
  )

kable(pct_ref_table |> mutate(across(starts_with("r_"), ~round(.x, 2))),
      caption = "r needed to reach a given % of each dimension's own saturated effect (bootstrap r-sweep) -- percentages are of the anchor metric's own value range (`R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP`), not a linear split of r")
```

```{r p2-pct-triples}
# Full factorial over {0,50,100}% x 3 dimensions (3^3 = 27 combinations),
# minus (0,0,0) -- that baseline is added separately wherever needed (e.g.
# line ~558, ~885) as the literal triple_id = 0 row, so it's excluded here
# to avoid a duplicate. The 2 "all-equal" diagonal combinations are placed
# first as triple_id 1/2, since two call sites below (attract_triples, the
# N-sensitivity r_label table) select them by literal triple_id %in% c(1,2).
pct_levels   <- c(0, 50, 100)
diag_triples <- tibble(pct_op = c(50, 100), pct_pw = c(50, 100), pct_tr = c(50, 100))
other_triples <- tidyr::crossing(pct_op = pct_levels, pct_pw = pct_levels, pct_tr = pct_levels) |>
  filter(!(pct_op == 0 & pct_pw == 0 & pct_tr == 0)) |>
  anti_join(diag_triples, by = c("pct_op", "pct_pw", "pct_tr"))
pct_triples <- bind_rows(diag_triples, other_triples) |>
  mutate(triple_id = row_number(), .before = 1)

r_triples <- pct_triples |>
  mutate(
    r_op = pct_to_r_from_anchor("op", pct_op, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_pw = pct_to_r_from_anchor("pw", pct_pw, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_tr = pct_to_r_from_anchor("tr", pct_tr, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP)
  )

kable(r_triples |> mutate(across(starts_with(c("pct_", "r_")), ~round(.x, 2))),
      caption = sprintf("The %d fixed effect-percentage combinations used below, translated to r via the bootstrap r-sweep (same per-dimension metric as the table above)", nrow(pct_triples)))
```

Each row is one $(pct_{op}, pct_{pw}, pct_{tr})$ combination from the full
factorial over $\{0, 50, 100\}$% (3^3 = 27 combinations), minus
$(0,0,0)$ -- that baseline is added separately wherever needed as its own
row. Report 22 used only 10 hand-picked combinations from a finer
$\{0,33,66,100\}$% cube; here all `r nrow(pct_triples)` remaining
combinations of the coarser $\{0,50,100\}$% grid are swept instead, so the
K-decision envelope (min/max across triples, Sec 2.3/2.5) reflects the
true worst case across the full percentage space rather than a hand-picked
subset of it, at a lower combinatorial cost than the finer grid.

## 2.3 First calibration of K

```{r p2-warmup-configs}
# Hardcoded, not CHOSEN_T_FINAL/CHOSEN_NV_FINAL: those are only defined
# later (Sec 3.2), after this K-decision step runs -- kept numerically in
# sync with the current choice (T=80, nv=40) by hand instead.
WARMUP_CONFIGS <- tribble(
  ~warmup_label, ~T_warmup, ~nv_warmup,
  "T=80, nv=40",  80L,       40L
)
LAMBDA_WARMUP <- 0.1
kable(WARMUP_CONFIGS)
```

```{r p2-config}
K_SWEEP_THRESH <- seq(30, 140, by = 10)
A_THRESHOLD <- 1   # A_ii, always exactly 1 -- see 2.1
QUALIFY_TOLERANCES <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)   # A_ij >= tolerance * A_ii, compared side by side below

# Placeholder used by the Sec 5 iteration loop and everywhere else only ONE
# tolerance is needed (not the 3-way comparison). Review the 2.5 plot/2.6
# table first, then update this by hand -- same "eyeball, then hardcode"
# spirit as CHOSEN_NV_FINAL/CHOSEN_DT_FINAL in Sec 3.
CHOSEN_TOLERANCE <- 0.5

# Decision criterion switched from the Dunbar & Spoors lower bound (12) to
# their mean (16) -- K now has to clear 16 qualifying neighbours, not 12.
TARGET_QUALIFYING <- 16
LOWER_BOUND_QUALIFYING <- 12
UPPER_BOUND_QUALIFYING <- 20

N_SEEDS_K <- 10L
N_THRESH  <- 1000L
```

```{r p2-fn}
count_qualifying_cell <- function(seed, K, triple_id, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, T_warmup, nv_warmup, tolerance) {
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = N_THRESH, n_communities = 1, node_degree = K, T = T_warmup,
    n_voting_rounds = nv_warmup,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_WARMUP, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05
  )
  gF  <- res$friendship_graph
  op  <- res$agents$opinion
  pow <- res$agents$power
  tau_list <- res$tau_final
  n_all <- nrow(res$agents)

  qualifying_counts <- vapply(seq_len(n_all), function(i) {
    nb <- as.integer(neighbors(gF, i, mode = "out"))
    if (!length(nb)) return(0L)
    a_op_pw   <- attractiveness_expose(op[i], op[nb], pow[i], pow[nb], r_op, r_pw)
    trust_mod <- if (!is.null(tau_list)) 2 * .sig(r_tr * (tau_list[[i]] - 1)) else 1
    sum(a_op_pw * trust_mod >= tolerance * A_THRESHOLD)
  }, integer(1L))

  tibble(seed = seed, K = K, triple_id = triple_id, tolerance = tolerance, mean_qualifying = mean(qualifying_counts))
}

run_k_decision <- function(r_triples_in, cache_tag) {
  grid_thresh <- tidyr::crossing(K = K_SWEEP_THRESH, triple_id = r_triples_in$triple_id,
                                  tolerance = QUALIFY_TOLERANCES, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_K)) |>
    left_join(r_triples_in, by = "triple_id")

  run_warmup_pass <- function(T_warmup, nv_warmup, cache_suffix) {
    run_cached(paste0("r23k_thresh_", cache_tag, "_", cache_suffix), function() {
      plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
      out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_thresh, function(K, triple_id, tolerance, seed, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, ...)
        count_qualifying_cell(seed, K, triple_id, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, T_warmup, nv_warmup, tolerance),
        .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
      plan(sequential)
      out
    }, list(grid_thresh, T_warmup, nv_warmup, A_THRESHOLD, N_THRESH, v = 1))
  }

  thresh_raw_all <- WARMUP_CONFIGS |>
    purrr::pmap(function(warmup_label, T_warmup, nv_warmup) {
      run_warmup_pass(T_warmup, nv_warmup, gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", warmup_label)) |>
        mutate(warmup_label = warmup_label)
    }) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    mutate(warmup_label = factor(warmup_label, levels = WARMUP_CONFIGS$warmup_label))

  thresh_per_triple <- thresh_raw_all |>
    group_by(warmup_label, tolerance, K, triple_id) |>
    summarise(mean_over_seeds = mean(mean_qualifying), .groups = "drop")

  thresh_summary <- thresh_per_triple |>
    group_by(warmup_label, tolerance, K) |>
    summarise(mean_val = mean(mean_over_seeds), min_val = min(mean_over_seeds),
              max_val = max(mean_over_seeds), sd_val = sd(mean_over_seeds), .groups = "drop")

  # Full decision table across all 3 tolerances x 2 warm-up lengths -- for
  # eyeballing/comparison (Sec 2.6).
  decision_by_warmup <- thresh_summary |>
    group_by(warmup_label, tolerance) |>
    group_modify(~ {
      clearing <- .x |> filter(mean_val >= TARGET_QUALIFYING) |> pull(K)
      reached  <- length(clearing) > 0
      tibble(target_reached = reached,
             chosen_k = if (reached) min(clearing) else max(K_SWEEP_THRESH),
             max_qualifying = max(.x$mean_val))
    }) |>
    ungroup()

  # Single-K decision at CHOSEN_TOLERANCE only -- this is what actually
  # feeds K forward (Sec 5 loop etc.), same logic as Report 22 otherwise.
  decision_chosen_tol <- decision_by_warmup |> filter(tolerance == CHOSEN_TOLERANCE)
  warmups_agree <- length(unique(decision_chosen_tol$chosen_k)) == 1 && all(decision_chosen_tol$target_reached)
  chosen_k <- if (warmups_agree) decision_chosen_tol$chosen_k[1] else max(decision_chosen_tol$chosen_k)

  triple_diagnostic <- thresh_per_triple |>
    filter(tolerance == CHOSEN_TOLERANCE) |>
    left_join(r_triples_in, by = "triple_id") |>
    group_by(across(any_of(c("triple_id", "pct_op", "pct_pw", "pct_tr", "r_op", "r_pw", "r_tr")))) |>
    summarise(reached_target = any(mean_over_seeds >= TARGET_QUALIFYING),
              max_qualifying = max(mean_over_seeds), .groups = "drop")

  list(CHOSEN_K = chosen_k, WARMUPS_AGREE = warmups_agree,
       decision_table = decision_by_warmup, thresh_summary = thresh_summary,
       thresh_per_triple = thresh_per_triple, triple_diagnostic = triple_diagnostic,
       r_triples = r_triples_in, N_R_TRIPLES = nrow(r_triples_in))
}
```

```{r p2-run}
k_res0 <- run_k_decision(r_triples, "iter0")
thresh_summary     <- k_res0$thresh_summary
decision_by_warmup <- k_res0$decision_table
WARMUPS_AGREE      <- k_res0$WARMUPS_AGREE
CHOSEN_K_22        <- k_res0$CHOSEN_K
N_R_TRIPLES        <- k_res0$N_R_TRIPLES
```

## 2.4 Neighbour attractiveness distribution (diagnostic)

Distribution of $A_{ij} \times \text{trust\_mod}$ across a random sample of
agents' out-neighbours, for two of the effect-percentage triples from 2.2 --
this is what `tolerance` actually cuts against in 2.5/2.6.

```{r p25-attract-fn}
sample_attractiveness <- function(seed, K, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, T_warmup, nv_warmup, n_agents = 30) {
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = N_THRESH, n_communities = 1, node_degree = K, T = T_warmup,
    n_voting_rounds = nv_warmup,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_WARMUP, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05
  )
  gF       <- res$friendship_graph
  op       <- res$agents$opinion
  pow      <- res$agents$power
  tau_list <- res$tau_final
  n_all    <- nrow(res$agents)

  set.seed(seed)
  sample_ids <- sample.int(n_all, min(n_agents, n_all))

  purrr::map_dfr(sample_ids, function(i) {
    nb <- as.integer(neighbors(gF, i, mode = "out"))
    if (!length(nb)) return(tibble())
    a_op_pw   <- attractiveness_expose(op[i], op[nb], pow[i], pow[nb], r_op, r_pw)
    trust_mod <- if (!is.null(tau_list)) 2 * .sig(r_tr * (tau_list[[i]] - 1)) else 1
    tibble(agent = i, attractiveness = a_op_pw * trust_mod)
  })
}
```

```{r p25-attract-run, fig.height=10}

attract_triples <- bind_rows(

  r_triples |> filter(triple_id %in% c(1, 2)),

attract_sample <- attract_triples |>
  purrr::pmap_dfr(function(triple_id, pct_op, pct_pw, pct_tr, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) {

    ) |>

  })

tol_lines <- tibble(tolerance = QUALIFY_TOLERANCES)

attract_sample |>

                           CHOSEN_K_22, length(unique(attract_sample$agent[attract_sample$triple_label == attract_sample$triple_label[1]])),
                           paste(QUALIFY_TOLERANCES, collapse = "/")),
```

# 3. T/n_voting_rounds sweep (manual read-off, not auto-picked)

Report 22 auto-picked (T, nv, Δt) from the saturation sweep below. Here the
sweep is only for visual inspection -- nv/Δt are chosen by eye afterwards
(Sec 3.2) and may be adjusted by hand again later.

```{r p2b-config}
DT_CANDIDATES <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10)
NV_SWEEP      <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60)

# r_op/r_pw/r_tr are held equal in PERCENTAGE terms (0/50/100% of each
# dimension's own saturated effect, via R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP), not in raw
# r terms -- each dimension's own saturated effect differs wildly in raw r
# (op ~16384, pw ~64, tr ~128 at the bootstrap config), so a single shared
# raw r_level (as this used to be, e.g. r=32 for all three) meant something
# very different per dimension. One row per r_pct, r_op/r_pw/r_tr computed
# together so they stay paired when crossed against nv/dt below.
R_PCT_SETTINGS <- c(0, 50, 100)
R_LEVELS_T <- tibble(r_pct = R_PCT_SETTINGS) |>
  mutate(
    r_op = pct_to_r_from_anchor("op", r_pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_pw = pct_to_r_from_anchor("pw", r_pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_tr = pct_to_r_from_anchor("tr", r_pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP)
  )

N_SEEDS_T <- 15L
```

```{r p2b-fn}
run_nv_dt_cell <- function(seed, nv, dt, r_pct, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, K_val, lambda_val = LAMBDA_CONTEXT) {
  T_val  <- nv * dt
  window <- max(1, T_val - 4):T_val
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = N_BASE, n_communities = 1, node_degree = K_val,
    T = T_val, n_voting_rounds = nv,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = lambda_val, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05,
    snap_rounds = window
  )
  snap_idx <- match(window, res$snapshots$round)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, nv = nv, dt = dt, r_pct = r_pct,
    delegation_rate      = mean(res$history_delegation[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    lost_vote_rate       = mean(res$history_lost[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    delegation_stability = mean(res$history_stability[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    chain_length         = mean(res$snapshots$avg_chain_length_delegators[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    top5_power_share     = mean(res$snapshots$top5_power_share[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct          = mean(res$snapshots$share_50pct[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# Pure sweep for visual inspection -- no auto-pick (see Sec 3 intro).
# levels_tbl defaults to R_LEVELS_T (0/50/100%) but takes a different
# r_pct/r_op/r_pw/r_tr tibble for the closer-look sweep below (25/50/75%).
run_t_sweep <- function(K_val, cache_tag, levels_tbl = R_LEVELS_T) {
  grid_nv_dt <- tidyr::crossing(nv = NV_SWEEP, dt = DT_CANDIDATES, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_T), levels_tbl)

  t_calib_raw <- run_cached(sprintf("r23t_sweep_%s_seeds%d", cache_tag, N_SEEDS_T), function() {
    plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
    out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_nv_dt, function(nv, dt, r_pct, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, seed)
      run_nv_dt_cell(seed, nv, dt, r_pct, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, K_val),
      .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
    plan(sequential)
    out
  }, list(grid_nv_dt, K_val, N_BASE, LAMBDA_CONTEXT, N_SEEDS_T, v = 1))

  t_calib_raw |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_core), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
    group_by(nv, dt, r_pct, metric) |>
    summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels[metrics_core])))
}
```

```{r p2b-run}
t_summary <- run_t_sweep(CHOSEN_K_22, "iter0")

# Closer look around r=50%: in the main plot below, all three r_pct columns
# share one y-axis per row (facet_grid's free_y frees per ROW, not per
# panel) -- at r=0%/100% several metrics sit pinned near their floor/ceiling,
# which forces that shared axis wide and visually flattens the (real, and
# similarly-sized) variation in the r=50% column. This second sweep at
# 25/50/75% is plotted with a genuinely independent scale per panel instead
# (facet_wrap, not facet_grid) so that variation is actually visible.
R_PCT_CLOSER <- c(25, 50, 75)
R_LEVELS_T_CLOSER <- tibble(r_pct = R_PCT_CLOSER) |>
  mutate(
    r_op = pct_to_r_from_anchor("op", r_pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_pw = pct_to_r_from_anchor("pw", r_pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
    r_tr = pct_to_r_from_anchor("tr", r_pct, bootstrap_r_res$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP)
  )
t_summary_closer <- run_t_sweep(CHOSEN_K_22, "iter0_closer", levels_tbl = R_LEVELS_T_CLOSER)
```

```{r p2b-plot-closer-fn}
plot_t_calib_closer <- function(t_summary) {

    facet_wrap(vars(metric, r_pct), scales = "free_y", ncol = length(R_PCT_CLOSER),
               labeller = labeller(r_pct = function(x) sprintf("r=%s%%", x))) +
    labs(title = "n_v / Δt sweep -- closer look around r=50%",
         subtitle = sprintf("K=%d, N=%d, %d seed(s) per cell; each panel independently scaled (facet_wrap, not facet_grid) so its own variation is visible regardless of the other columns",
                             CHOSEN_K_22, N_BASE, N_SEEDS_T),
         x = "n_v (voting rounds)", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top") + FACET_SPACING
}
```

## 3.2 Manual choice

```{r p2b-fixed}

CHOSEN_NV_FINAL <- 40
CHOSEN_DT_FINAL <- 2
CHOSEN_T_FINAL  <- CHOSEN_NV_FINAL * CHOSEN_DT_FINAL
```

**Chosen: T=`r CHOSEN_T_FINAL`, n_v=`r CHOSEN_NV_FINAL`, Δt=`r CHOSEN_DT_FINAL`.**

# 4. Responsiveness-range saturation ($r_{op}, r_{pw}, r_{tr}$)

K is fixed at `r CHOSEN_K_22` (Sec 2, provisional first guess -- refined in Sec 5);
T=`r CHOSEN_T_FINAL`, nv=`r CHOSEN_NV_FINAL`, Δt=`r CHOSEN_DT_FINAL` (fixed above, Sec 3.2).

## 4.2 Isolated dimensions ($r_{op}$, $r_{pw}$, $r_{tr}$ swept alone)


"Delta %" columns = step-to-step change as a % of that metric's own
observed range (max-min across all r_val), not an absolute difference.

```{r p3-sat-anchor-manual}
# ANNAHME (placeholder, fill in by hand from the table above -- final K/T
# config, not the bootstrap K=40/T=30 one from Sec 2.2). Same
# eyeball-then-hardcode pattern as R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP. Placeholder
# defaults (full swept range, Delegation rate) keep this runnable before
# read-off; update both columns per dimension once the plot/table above
# have been checked. Feeds Sec 6's r ceilings and everything downstream
# that expresses r in percentages (Sec 7-10) via pct_to_r_from_anchor().
R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL <- tribble(
  ~dim,  ~r_sat,             ~r_sat_metric,
  "op",  max(R_OPTR_MAX),    "Delegation rate",
  "pw",  max(R_OPTR_MAX),    "Delegation rate",
  "tr",  max(R_OPTR_MAX),    "Delegation rate"
)

r_sat_manual_final <- function(d) R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL$r_sat[R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL$dim == d]
```

# 5. K/T/r first values (first run)

```{r p5-loop}
MAX_ITER <- 1L
K_TOL    <- 0

r_sweep_current <- bootstrap_r_res
iter_log  <- list()
k_prev    <- NA_integer_
converged <- FALSE

for (iter in 0:(MAX_ITER - 1)) {
  # iter=0 always reads r_sweep_current == bootstrap_r_res (assigned above),
  # so R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP is the right anchor here. NOTE: manual
  # eyeball-then-hardcode fundamentally doesn't extend to iter>0 -- a human
  # can't interactively re-read a table mid-loop -- so with MAX_ITER=1 this
  # is exact, but raising MAX_ITER later would need this rewired (e.g. to
  # R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL, itself re-read-off by hand between runs) rather than
  # left as-is.
  r_triples_current <- pct_triples |>
    mutate(
      r_op = pct_to_r_from_anchor("op", pct_op, r_sweep_current$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
      r_pw = pct_to_r_from_anchor("pw", pct_pw, r_sweep_current$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP),
      r_tr = pct_to_r_from_anchor("tr", pct_tr, r_sweep_current$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_BOOTSTRAP)
    )

  k_res <- run_k_decision(r_triples_current, paste0("iter", iter))
  r_res <- run_r_sweep(k_res$CHOSEN_K, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, paste0("iter", iter))

  iter_log[[iter + 1]] <- tibble(
    iter = iter, K = k_res$CHOSEN_K, T = CHOSEN_T_FINAL, NV = CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, DT = CHOSEN_DT_FINAL,
    tolerance = CHOSEN_TOLERANCE,
    r_sat_op = r_res$r_sat_isolated$r_sat[r_res$r_sat_isolated$dim == "op"],
    r_sat_pw = r_res$r_sat_isolated$r_sat[r_res$r_sat_isolated$dim == "pw"],
    r_sat_tr = r_res$r_sat_isolated$r_sat[r_res$r_sat_isolated$dim == "tr"]
  )

  if (iter > 0 && abs(k_res$CHOSEN_K - k_prev) <= K_TOL) { converged <- TRUE; break }

  k_prev <- k_res$CHOSEN_K
  r_sweep_current <- r_res
}

iter_table <- bind_rows(iter_log)
FINAL_ITER      <- iter
CHOSEN_K_FINAL  <- k_res$CHOSEN_K

# T/nv/dt are already fixed (Sec 3.2) and r_res above was already computed
# at CHOSEN_K_FINAL/CHOSEN_T_FINAL/CHOSEN_NV_FINAL directly -- no separate
# re-run needed, just carry it forward under a stable name.
r_res_final <- r_res
r_sat_FINAL <- r_res_final$r_sat_isolated
```

```{r p5-table}
kable(iter_table |> mutate(across(starts_with("r_sat"), ~round(.x, 3))),
      caption = "K/T/r across loop iterations")
```

```{r p5-prose, results = "asis"}
if (converged) {
  cat(sprintf("**K converged after %d iterations**: K=%d agreed between iteration %d and iteration %d.",
              FINAL_ITER + 1, CHOSEN_K_FINAL, FINAL_ITER - 1, FINAL_ITER))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("**K did NOT converge within %d iterations** (K sequence: %s) -- the iteration-%d values below are reported as provisional, not converged. Raise MAX_ITER (and the seed counts, currently 1 for a fast first pass) to close the loop properly.",
              MAX_ITER, paste(iter_table$K, collapse = " -> "), FINAL_ITER))
}
```

# 7. N sensitivity check

```{r p8-config}
N_SENS_GRID   <- c(1500, 3000, 6000, 12000)
N_SEEDS_N     <- 10L

N_SENS_TRIPLES <- bind_rows(
  tibble(triple_id = 0, r_op = 0, r_pw = 0, r_tr = 0, r_label = "r=r=r 0%"),
  r_triples |> filter(triple_id %in% c(1, 2)) |>
    transmute(triple_id, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, r_label = sprintf("r=r=r %d%%", pct_op))
)
```

```{r p8-fn}
run_n_cell <- function(seed, N, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) {
  window <- max(1, CHOSEN_T_FINAL - 4):CHOSEN_T_FINAL
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = N, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K_FINAL, T = CHOSEN_T_FINAL,
    n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_NV_FINAL,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_CONTEXT, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05,
    snap_rounds = window
  )
  snap_idx <- match(window, res$snapshots$round)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, N = N,
    delegation_rate      = mean(res$history_delegation[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    delegation_stability = mean(res$history_stability[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    lost_vote_rate       = mean(res$history_lost[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    top5_power_share     = mean(res$snapshots$top5_power_share[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct          = mean(res$snapshots$share_50pct[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    chain_length         = mean(res$snapshots$avg_chain_length_delegators[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}
```

```{r p8-run}
grid_n_sens <- tidyr::crossing(N_SENS_TRIPLES, N = N_SENS_GRID, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_N))

n_sens_raw <- run_cached("r23n_sensitivity", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_n_sens, function(triple_id, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, r_label, N, seed)
    run_n_cell(seed, N, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) |> mutate(triple_id = triple_id, r_label = r_label, .before = 1),
    .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(grid_n_sens, CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, LAMBDA_CONTEXT, v = 1))

n_sens_summary <- n_sens_raw |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_r), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(r_label, N, metric) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels[metrics_r])))
```

```{r p8-plot, fig.height=9}
n_sens_summary |>

  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "r_op=r_pw=r_tr level", end = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "N sensitivity at calibrated K/T/nv",
       subtitle = sprintf("K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d, %d seed(s) per point; small-world corridor requires N > %d",
                           CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, N_SEEDS_N, N_MIN_CORRIDOR),
```

# 8. Δt x λ (trust forget-rate) interaction

```{r p9-config}
FORGET_RATES  <- c(10, 50, 90)
LAMBDA_VALUES <- lambda_from_forget_rate(FORGET_RATES)
names(LAMBDA_VALUES) <- sprintf("forget%d", FORGET_RATES)

n_voting_rounds_in_window <- function(T_val, nv, window = 5) {
  voting_rounds <- round(seq(T_val / nv, T_val, length.out = nv))
  sum(voting_rounds > T_val - window)
}

N_SEEDS_S9   <- 10L
# 50% row of R_LEVELS_T (Sec 3) -- reusing the same bootstrap-derived
# percentage translation rather than recomputing it here.
R_LEVEL_FOR_DTLAMBDA <- R_LEVELS_T |> filter(r_pct == 50)
```

```{r p9-default-ref, results = "asis"}
default_forget_rate <- LAMBDA_FORGET_PCT_5

lo <- FORGET_RATES[FORGET_RATES <= default_forget_rate]
hi <- FORGET_RATES[FORGET_RATES >= default_forget_rate]

if (any(FORGET_RATES == default_forget_rate)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "For reference: the report's own default `LAMBDA_CONTEXT = %.4f` corresponds to **%.1f%% forgotten after 5 voting rounds**, which matches the `forget%d` column below exactly.",
    LAMBDA_CONTEXT, default_forget_rate, default_forget_rate
  ))
} else if (!length(lo)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "For reference: the report's own default `LAMBDA_CONTEXT = %.4f` corresponds to **%.1f%% forgotten after 5 voting rounds** -- this falls BELOW the lowest swept forget-rate (`forget%d`), so no sweep column below reproduces the report's actual working default.",
    LAMBDA_CONTEXT, default_forget_rate, min(FORGET_RATES)
  ))
} else if (!length(hi)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "For reference: the report's own default `LAMBDA_CONTEXT = %.4f` corresponds to **%.1f%% forgotten after 5 voting rounds** -- this falls ABOVE the highest swept forget-rate (`forget%d`), so no sweep column below reproduces the report's actual working default.",
    LAMBDA_CONTEXT, default_forget_rate, max(FORGET_RATES)
  ))
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "For reference: the report's own default `LAMBDA_CONTEXT = %.4f` corresponds to **%.1f%% forgotten after 5 voting rounds** -- this falls between the `forget%d` and `forget%d` columns below, not at either one, so neither sweep column should be read as reproducing the report's actual working default.",
    LAMBDA_CONTEXT, default_forget_rate, max(lo), min(hi)
  ))
}
```

# 9. Self-reliance c sensitivity

`self_reliance_c` (the c in the Möbius self-vote curve `p_self_mobius_M`,
Sec 1.4.1) swept across its full [0, 1] range, over all six tracked metrics,
at three r_op=r_pw=r_tr levels (0%, 50%, 100% of each dimension's own
saturated effect, single shared dial like Sec 7/10) shown as separate
coloured lines per facet. Note: c=0 is a genuine division-by-zero in
`p_self_mobius_M` (`(M-1)/c` blows up), so the sweep uses c=0.01 as the
practical lower bound instead of the literal 0.

```{r p10-c-config}
C_SWEEP      <- c(0.01, seq(0.1, 1, by = 0.1))
N_SEEDS_S10  <- 25L

C_R_LEVELS <- bind_rows(
  tibble(r_pct = 0, r_op = 0, r_pw = 0, r_tr = 0),
  tibble(r_pct = c(50, 100)) |>
    mutate(
      r_op = pct_to_r_from_anchor("op", r_pct, r_res_final$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL),
      r_pw = pct_to_r_from_anchor("pw", r_pct, r_res_final$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL),
      r_tr = pct_to_r_from_anchor("tr", r_pct, r_res_final$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL)
    )
)
```

```{r p10-c-run}
c_sweep_cell <- function(seed, c_val, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) {
  window <- max(1, CHOSEN_T_FINAL - 4):CHOSEN_T_FINAL
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = N_BASE, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K_FINAL,
    T = CHOSEN_T_FINAL, n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_NV_FINAL,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_CONTEXT, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = c_val, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05,
    snap_rounds = window
  )
  snap_idx <- match(window, res$snapshots$round)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, c_val = c_val,
    delegation_rate      = mean(res$history_delegation[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    delegation_stability = mean(res$history_stability[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    lost_vote_rate       = mean(res$history_lost[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    chain_length         = mean(res$snapshots$avg_chain_length_delegators[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    top5_power_share     = mean(res$snapshots$top5_power_share[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct          = mean(res$snapshots$share_50pct[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

grid_c <- tidyr::crossing(C_R_LEVELS, c_val = C_SWEEP, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_S10))
c_sweep_raw <- run_cached("r23_s10_c_sweep", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_c, function(c_val, r_pct, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, seed)
    c_sweep_cell(seed, c_val, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) |> mutate(r_pct = r_pct),
    .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(grid_c, CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, v = 1))

c_sweep_summary <- c_sweep_raw |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_core), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(c_val, r_pct, metric) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), se_val = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels[metrics_core])),
         r_level = factor(sprintf("r=r=r %d%%", r_pct), levels = sprintf("r=r=r %d%%", c(0, 50, 100))))
```

```{r p10-c-plot, fig.height=9}
             aes(x = x, y = y), inherit.aes = FALSE) +

                           CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, N_SEEDS_S10),
```

# 10. Watts-Strogatz vs. Barabasi-Albert

Fixing N=`r N_BASE`, K=`r CHOSEN_K_FINAL`, T=`r CHOSEN_T_FINAL`, nv=`r CHOSEN_NV_FINAL`
(the calibrated values from Sec. 6, not `Report_20`'s anchor N=1000/K=16): does
the network generator itself matter? WS (small-world, the default used
everywhere else in this report) vs. BA (Barabasi-Albert preferential
attachment -- hub-like degree heterogeneity that WS cannot produce). Everything
from here on is expressed in r-percentages (% of each dimension's own
saturated effect, read off by hand into `R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL`, Sec 4.2), not
raw r-values -- consistent with Sec 7/9. Each pair of responsiveness dimensions is varied
*together* across 10%-100% (in 10-point steps) of their own saturated effect,
while the third is held fixed at one of three levels (0%/50%/100%), shown as
differently coloured lines, network type distinguished by line style on top
of that (WS solid, BA dashed). All three possible pairings are covered:

- $r_{op}=r_{pw}$ varied, $r_{tr}$ fixed
- $r_{op}=r_{tr}$ varied, $r_{pw}$ fixed
- $r_{pw}=r_{tr}$ varied, $r_{op}$ fixed

```{r p11-config}
PCT_VALS_WSBA         <- seq(10, 100, by = 10)
PCT_FIXED_LEVELS_WSBA <- c(0, 50, 100)
N_SEEDS_WSBA          <- 25L
```

```{r p11-fn}
run_wsba_cell <- function(seed, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, network_type) {
  window <- max(1, CHOSEN_T_FINAL - 4):CHOSEN_T_FINAL
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = N_BASE, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K_FINAL,
    T = CHOSEN_T_FINAL, n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, network_type = network_type,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_CONTEXT, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05,
    snap_rounds = window
  )
  snap_idx <- match(window, res$snapshots$round)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, network_type = network_type,
    delegation_rate      = mean(res$history_delegation[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    delegation_stability = mean(res$history_stability[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    lost_vote_rate       = mean(res$history_lost[window], na.rm = TRUE),
    chain_length         = mean(res$snapshots$avg_chain_length_delegators[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    top5_power_share     = mean(res$snapshots$top5_power_share[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct          = mean(res$snapshots$share_50pct[snap_idx], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

build_wsba_pair_grid <- function(pair_label, dim_v1, dim_v2, dim_f) {
  df <- tidyr::crossing(pct_v = PCT_VALS_WSBA, pct_f = PCT_FIXED_LEVELS_WSBA,
                         network_type = c("ws", "ba"), seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_WSBA))
  df$pair_label <- pair_label
  r_v1 <- pct_to_r_from_anchor(dim_v1, df$pct_v, r_res_final$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL)
  r_v2 <- pct_to_r_from_anchor(dim_v2, df$pct_v, r_res_final$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL)
  r_f  <- pct_to_r_from_anchor(dim_f,  df$pct_f, r_res_final$r3_isolated_final, R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL)
  r_by_dim <- setNames(list(r_v1, r_v2, r_f), c(dim_v1, dim_v2, dim_f))
  df$r_op <- r_by_dim[["op"]]
  df$r_pw <- r_by_dim[["pw"]]
  df$r_tr <- r_by_dim[["tr"]]
  df
}
```

```{r p11-run}
grid_wsba <- bind_rows(
  build_wsba_pair_grid("r_op x r_pw (r_tr fixed)", "op", "pw", "tr"),
  build_wsba_pair_grid("r_op x r_tr (r_pw fixed)", "op", "tr", "pw"),
  build_wsba_pair_grid("r_pw x r_tr (r_op fixed)", "pw", "tr", "op")
)

wsba_raw <- run_cached("r23_wsba_pair", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_wsba, function(pair_label, pct_v, pct_f, network_type, seed, r_op, r_pw, r_tr)
    run_wsba_cell(seed, r_op, r_pw, r_tr, network_type) |> mutate(pair_label = pair_label, pct_v = pct_v, pct_f = pct_f),
    .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(grid_wsba, CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, LAMBDA_CONTEXT, v = 2))

wsba_summary <- wsba_raw |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_core), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(pair_label, network_type, pct_v, pct_f, metric) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels[metrics_core])),
         network_type = factor(network_type, levels = c("ws", "ba"), labels = c("WS", "BA")))
```

```{r p11-plot-fn}
plot_wsba_pair <- function(label) {
  wsba_summary |>
    filter(pair_label == label) |>
    ggplot(aes(pct_v, mean_val, colour = factor(pct_f, levels = PCT_FIXED_LEVELS_WSBA),
               linetype = network_type, group = interaction(pct_f, network_type))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = PCT_VALS_WSBA) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "fixed level (%)", end = 0.85) +
    scale_linetype_manual(name = "network", values = c(WS = "solid", BA = "dashed")) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    labs(title = sprintf("K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d -- %s x network", CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, label),
         subtitle = sprintf("%d seeds per cell; shared axis and fixed level both in %% of each dimension's own saturated effect", N_SEEDS_WSBA),
         x = "shared r level (% of each dimension's own saturated effect)", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top") + FACET_SPACING
}
```

Runtime for a single simulation at the final calibrated config (K=`r CHOSEN_K_FINAL`, T=`r CHOSEN_T_FINAL`, nv=`r CHOSEN_NV_FINAL`, N=`r N_BASE`): **`r sprintf("%.2f", single_run_time_sec)` seconds**.

```{r p12-timing-per-section}
describe_cache <- function(cache_name) {
  case_when(
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23r_isolated_raw_fine_bootstrap") ~
      sprintf("r-sweep bootstrap, fine grid (K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d)", K_BOOTSTRAP, T_BOOTSTRAP, NV_BOOTSTRAP),
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23r_isolated_raw_bootstrap") ~
      sprintf("r-sweep bootstrap, coarse grid (K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d)", K_BOOTSTRAP, T_BOOTSTRAP, NV_BOOTSTRAP),
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23r_isolated_raw_fine_iter") ~
      sprintf("r-sweep at chosen K, fine grid (K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d)", CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL),
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23r_isolated_raw_iter") ~
      sprintf("r-sweep at chosen K, coarse grid (K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d)", CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL),
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23k_thresh_") ~
      sprintf("K-sweep (K=%d-%d, T=%d, nv=%d, %d r-triples x %d tolerances)",
              min(K_SWEEP_THRESH), max(K_SWEEP_THRESH),
              WARMUP_CONFIGS$T_warmup[1], WARMUP_CONFIGS$nv_warmup[1],
              nrow(r_triples), length(QUALIFY_TOLERANCES)),
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23t_sweep_") ~
      sprintf("T/nv sweep (K=%d, nv up to %d, dt up to %d)", CHOSEN_K_22, max(NV_SWEEP), max(DT_CANDIDATES)),
    cache_name == "r23n_sensitivity" ~
      sprintf("N sensitivity (K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d, N up to %d)", CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, max(N_SENS_GRID)),
    cache_name == "r23_dtlambda" ~
      sprintf("dt x lambda (K=%d, nv up to %d, dt up to %d)", CHOSEN_K_FINAL, max(NV_SWEEP), max(DT_CANDIDATES)),
    cache_name == "r23_s10_c_sweep" ~
      sprintf("Self-reliance c (K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d)", CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL),
    cache_name == "r23_wsba_pair" ~
      sprintf("WS vs BA (K=%d, T=%d, nv=%d)", CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL),
    TRUE ~ cache_name
  )
}

# Seeds per grid cell for each sweep -- same dispatch/patterns as
# describe_cache() above, so the two always agree on which cache is which.
n_seeds_for_cache <- function(cache_name) {
  case_when(
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23r_isolated_raw_") ~ N_SEEDS_R,
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23k_thresh_")       ~ N_SEEDS_K,
    str_starts(cache_name, "r23t_sweep_")        ~ N_SEEDS_T,
    cache_name == "r23n_sensitivity"             ~ N_SEEDS_N,
    cache_name == "r23_dtlambda"                 ~ N_SEEDS_S9,
    cache_name == "r23_s10_c_sweep"              ~ N_SEEDS_S10,
    cache_name == "r23_wsba_pair"                ~ N_SEEDS_WSBA,
    TRUE ~ NA_integer_
  )
}

timing_log_df <- bind_rows(TIMING_LOG) |>
  mutate(description = describe_cache(cache_name),
         seeds   = n_seeds_for_cache(cache_name),
         minutes = round(seconds / 60, 1)) |>
  select(Sweep = description, Status = status, Seeds = seeds, Runs = n_rows, Seconds = seconds, Minutes = minutes)

kable(timing_log_df, caption = "Actual measured wall-clock time per sweep this knit -- 'cached' rows took 0s because they were reused from a previous run's saved .rds, not recomputed. Seeds = seeds per grid cell; Runs = total `simulate_liquid_democracy()` calls (grid cells x seeds) that sweep represents, whether cached or freshly computed this knit")
```

# 12. RQ1-3: Effect of Responsiveness on Liquid Democracy Outcomes

Formerly its own standalone report (RQ1.Rmd), kept in sync with this
document's K/T/n_v/λ by hand. Now appended here directly: reuses
`CHOSEN_K_FINAL`, `CHOSEN_T_FINAL`, `CHOSEN_NV_FINAL`, `LAMBDA_CONTEXT` from
Sec. 6 instead of a separate copy of the same constants.

```{r rq-metrics-setup}
# RQ1: delegation behaviour. RQ2: quality of representation (ideological
# drift). RQ3: concentration of voting power. All three are answered off the
# SAME simulation grid (see 12.2 below) -- one run per (pair, fixed-level,
# seed) cell produces every metric needed for all three RQs at once.
metrics_rq1 <- c("delegation_rate", "lost_vote_rate", "n_direct_voters", "chain_length", "flickerness")
metrics_rq2 <- c("avg_drift")
metrics_rq3 <- c("top5_power_share", "share_50pct")
metrics_all_rqs <- c(metrics_rq1, metrics_rq2, metrics_rq3)

# _rq suffix: this report already has its own metric_labels (Sec 1) for a
# different metric set -- kept separate rather than overloading that name.
metric_labels_rq <- c(
  delegation_rate  = "Delegation rate",
  lost_vote_rate   = "Lost-vote rate",
  n_direct_voters  = "Direct voters (N x (1 - delegation rate))",
  chain_length     = "Avg. delegation-chain length",
  flickerness      = "Flickerness (delegation-target stability)",
  avg_drift        = "Avg. ideological drift",
  top5_power_share = "Top-5% voting-power share",
  share_50pct      = "Agents needed for 50% of power"
)

# r_op/r_pw/r_tr needed to reach a given % of each dimension's own saturated
# effect -- the specific, already-confirmed numbers given for this section
# (not tied to R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL above, which may still be a placeholder --
# see Sec 4.2's own comment). Linearly interpolated for pct in between.
RQ_PCT_LOOKUP <- tribble(
  ~pct, ~r_op,     ~r_pw, ~r_tr,
  0,       0.00,     0.00,   0.00,
  10,     13.17,     0.05,   2.09,
  20,     28.85,     0.10,   3.99,
  30,     48.58,     0.15,   6.79,
  40,     72.89,     0.20,   9.76,
  50,    109.53,     0.32,  12.86,
  60,    166.16,     0.51,  15.97,
  70,    243.11,     1.07,  22.97,
  80,    429.31,     3.04,  30.01,
  90,    910.23,     6.59,  48.68,
  100, 16384.00,    64.00, 128.00
)

pct_to_r_rq <- function(dim_name, pct) {
  col <- switch(dim_name, op = "r_op", pw = "r_pw", tr = "r_tr", stop("unknown dim: ", dim_name))
  approx(RQ_PCT_LOOKUP$pct, RQ_PCT_LOOKUP[[col]], xout = pct, rule = 2)$y
}
```

**K = `r CHOSEN_K_FINAL`, T = `r CHOSEN_T_FINAL` (`r CHOSEN_NV_FINAL` voting
rounds, Δt = `r CHOSEN_DT_FINAL`), c = 0.5, forget rate = 50% over 5 voting
rounds (`LAMBDA_CONTEXT`).**

```{r rq-pct-table}
kable(RQ_PCT_LOOKUP, caption = "r needed to reach a given % of each dimension's own saturated effect -- everything below is expressed in these percentages, not raw r")
```

## 12.1 Extreme behaviour: single-dial vs. isolated dimensions, 0-100%

A wide look across the full 0-100% range of each dimension's own saturated
effect, fixed at N=`r N_BASE`, K=`r CHOSEN_K_FINAL` -- showing every metric
used in RQ1-3 below at once, to see where each one saturates. Four
scenarios: **all** ($r_{op},r_{pw},r_{tr}$ all at the same %, each
translated via `RQ_PCT_LOOKUP`) and each dimension **isolated** in turn (one
dimension at that %, the other two at 0).

```{r rq-extreme-config}
PCT_VALS_EXTREME <- seq(0, 100, by = 10)
N_SEEDS_EXTREME  <- 25L

scenarios_extreme <- tribble(
  ~scenario,     ~use_op, ~use_pw, ~use_tr,
  "all (r=r=r)", TRUE,    TRUE,    TRUE,
  "op only",     TRUE,    FALSE,   FALSE,
  "pw only",     FALSE,   TRUE,    FALSE,
  "trust only",  FALSE,   FALSE,   TRUE
)
```

```{r rq-extreme-run}
run_extreme_cell <- function(seed, pct, scenario, use_op, use_pw, use_tr) {
  r_op <- if (use_op) pct_to_r_rq("op", pct) else 0
  r_pw <- if (use_pw) pct_to_r_rq("pw", pct) else 0
  r_tr <- if (use_tr) pct_to_r_rq("tr", pct) else 0
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = N_BASE, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K_FINAL, T = CHOSEN_T_FINAL,
    n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_NV_FINAL,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_CONTEXT, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05
  )
  last5 <- max(1L, CHOSEN_T_FINAL - 4L):CHOSEN_T_FINAL
  snaps <- res$snapshots |> dplyr::filter(round >= max(1L, CHOSEN_T_FINAL - 4L))
  delegation_rate <- mean(res$history_delegation[last5], na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, pct = pct, scenario = scenario,
    delegation_rate  = delegation_rate,
    lost_vote_rate   = mean(res$history_lost[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    n_direct_voters  = N_BASE * (1 - delegation_rate),
    chain_length     = mean(snaps$avg_chain_length_delegators, na.rm = TRUE),
    flickerness      = mean(res$history_flickerness[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_drift        = mean(snaps$avg_drift, na.rm = TRUE),
    top5_power_share = mean(snaps$top5_power_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct      = mean(snaps$share_50pct, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

grid_extreme <- tidyr::crossing(scenarios_extreme, pct = PCT_VALS_EXTREME, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_EXTREME))

extreme_raw <- run_cached("rq_extreme_raw", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_extreme, run_extreme_cell, .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(N_BASE, CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, N_SEEDS_EXTREME, PCT_VALS_EXTREME,
        scenarios_extreme, LAMBDA_CONTEXT, RQ_PCT_LOOKUP, v = 1))

extreme_summary <- extreme_raw |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_all_rqs), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(scenario, pct, metric) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(metric   = factor(metric_labels_rq[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels_rq)),
         scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenarios_extreme$scenario))
```

```{r rq-extreme-plot, fig.height=12}
extreme_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, mean_val, colour = scenario, group = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = PCT_VALS_EXTREME) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "responsiveness scenario", end = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Extreme behaviour -- N=%d, K=%d, all vs. isolated dimensions", N_BASE, CHOSEN_K_FINAL),
       subtitle = sprintf("%d seeds per cell; x = %% of each dimension's own saturated effect (RQ_PCT_LOOKUP)", N_SEEDS_EXTREME),
       x = "% of own saturated effect", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 12.2 Shared design: paired sweep, third dimension held fixed

Same sweep grid for all three RQs. For each pair of responsiveness
dimensions, both are varied *together* in **percentage** terms (translated
to each dimension's own r via `RQ_PCT_LOOKUP` -- op/pw/tr saturate at
wildly different raw r, so a shared raw value wouldn't mean the same thing
across dimensions) across $\{10,20,...,100\}\%$, while the third dimension
is held fixed at one of 3 percentage levels ($0\%, 50\%, 100\%$) -- shown
as 3 coloured lines in the same plot. Repeating this for each of the 3
possible pairs gives 3 plots per RQ, covering all three responsiveness
dimensions:

- $r_{op}, r_{pw}$ varied together $\in \{10,...,100\}\%$, $r_{tr} \in \{0,50,100\}\%$ (fixed)
- $r_{op}, r_{tr}$ varied together $\in \{10,...,100\}\%$, $r_{pw} \in \{0,50,100\}\%$ (fixed)
- $r_{pw}, r_{tr}$ varied together $\in \{10,...,100\}\%$, $r_{op} \in \{0,50,100\}\%$ (fixed)

```{r rq-config}
N_SEEDS_PAIR <- 25L

PCT_VALS_PAIR    <- seq(10, 100, by = 10)  # % for the two paired (jointly varied) dimensions
PCT_FIXED_LEVELS <- c(0, 50, 100)          # % for the third, held-fixed dimension
```

```{r rq-pair-run}
build_pair_grid <- function(pair_label, dim_v1, dim_v2, dim_fixed) {
  df <- tidyr::crossing(pct_v = PCT_VALS_PAIR, pct_f = PCT_FIXED_LEVELS, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_PAIR))
  df$pair_label <- pair_label
  df[[paste0("r_", dim_v1)]]    <- pct_to_r_rq(dim_v1, df$pct_v)
  df[[paste0("r_", dim_v2)]]    <- pct_to_r_rq(dim_v2, df$pct_v)
  df[[paste0("r_", dim_fixed)]] <- pct_to_r_rq(dim_fixed, df$pct_f)
  df
}

grid_pair <- bind_rows(
  build_pair_grid("r_op x r_pw (r_tr fixed)", "op", "pw", "tr"),
  build_pair_grid("r_op x r_tr (r_pw fixed)", "op", "tr", "pw"),
  build_pair_grid("r_pw x r_tr (r_op fixed)", "pw", "tr", "op")
)

run_pair_cell <- function(seed, pair_label, pct_v, pct_f, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) {
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = 500L, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K_FINAL, T = CHOSEN_T_FINAL,
    n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_NV_FINAL,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_CONTEXT, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = 0.5, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05
  )
  last5 <- max(1L, CHOSEN_T_FINAL - 4L):CHOSEN_T_FINAL
  snaps <- res$snapshots |> dplyr::filter(round >= max(1L, CHOSEN_T_FINAL - 4L))
  delegation_rate <- mean(res$history_delegation[last5], na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, pair_label = pair_label, pct_v = pct_v, pct_f = pct_f,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, r_tr = r_tr,
    # RQ1
    delegation_rate  = delegation_rate,
    lost_vote_rate   = mean(res$history_lost[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    n_direct_voters  = 500L * (1 - delegation_rate),
    chain_length     = mean(snaps$avg_chain_length_delegators, na.rm = TRUE),
    flickerness      = mean(res$history_flickerness[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    # RQ2
    avg_drift        = mean(snaps$avg_drift, na.rm = TRUE),
    # RQ3
    top5_power_share = mean(snaps$top5_power_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct      = mean(snaps$share_50pct, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

pair_raw <- run_cached("rq123_pair_raw", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_pair, run_pair_cell, .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(CHOSEN_K_FINAL, CHOSEN_T_FINAL, CHOSEN_NV_FINAL, N_SEEDS_PAIR, PCT_VALS_PAIR, PCT_FIXED_LEVELS, LAMBDA_CONTEXT, RQ_PCT_LOOKUP, v = 1))

pair_summary <- pair_raw |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_all_rqs), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(pair_label, pct_v, pct_f, metric) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels_rq[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels_rq)))

# metrics_subset selects which of the 8 metrics (as their metric_labels_rq)
# go into this particular plot -- each RQ section below passes its own subset.
plot_pair_rq <- function(label, metrics_subset) {
  pair_summary |>
    filter(pair_label == label, metric %in% metric_labels_rq[metrics_subset]) |>
    ggplot(aes(pct_v, mean_val, colour = factor(pct_f, levels = PCT_FIXED_LEVELS))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = PCT_VALS_PAIR) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "fixed level", end = 0.85, labels = function(x) sprintf("%s%%", x)) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Paired sweep -- %s", label),
         subtitle = sprintf("%d seeds per cell; values are %% of each dimension's own saturated effect (RQ_PCT_LOOKUP), not raw r", N_SEEDS_PAIR),
         x = "shared % of own saturated effect", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

## 12.3 RQ1: delegation behaviour

Metrics: delegation rate, lost-vote rate, number of direct voters, average
delegation-chain length, and flickerness (share of agents keeping the same
delegation target as the previous round -- `history_flickerness` from
`simulate_liquid_democracy()`, NA on round 1).

```{r rq1-pair-plot-1, fig.height=14}
plot_pair_rq("r_op x r_pw (r_tr fixed)", metrics_rq1)
```



## 12.4 RQ2: quality of political representation

Metric: average ideological drift (`avg_drift`) -- the mean distance between
an agent's own opinion and the opinion of the agent who ultimately casts a
vote on its behalf.

Expected: $r_{op}$ reduces drift; $r_{pw}$ increases drift (powerful
delegates stay attractive even when ideologically distant); $r_{tr}$
reduces drift, same mechanism as $r_{op}$.

```{r rq2-pair-plot-1, fig.height=6}

```

## 12.5 RQ3: concentration of voting power

Metrics: voting-power share held by the top 5% of agents (`top5_power_share`)
and the fraction of agents needed to collectively hold 50% of total voting
power (`share_50pct`).

Expected: $r_{op}$ lowers concentration (more agents vote directly);
$r_{pw}$ raises concentration (rich-get-richer). For the joint
$r_{op} \times r_{pw}$ effect: low opinion-based attractiveness is expected
to constrain how much high voting power can raise a neighbour's overall
attractiveness -- so increasing both together should yield *lower*
concentration than high $r_{pw}$ alone.
